smt-2013-advanced-tiebreaker-01.title: Look at Beth's last flip
smt-2013-advanced-tiebreaker-01.body:
Before Beth's last flip both have flipped $5$ times. Let $x$ be the probability they have equal head counts; by symmetry Andrew leads with probability $\frac{1-x}2$ and Beth leads with probability $\frac{1-x}2$. Then Beth's sixth flip: if Andrew leads he stays at least even; if tied he stays at least even only when Beth flips tails (probability $\frac12$); if Beth leads he never catches up. So

$$P=\frac{1-x}2+\frac x2+0=\frac12.$$

**Answer: $\frac12$**

smt-2013-advanced-tiebreaker-01.title: Turn it into one binomial
smt-2013-advanced-tiebreaker-01.body:
Let $A'$ be Andrew's number of tails ($5-A$ heads). $A\ge B\iff5-A'\ge B\iff A'+B\le5$. But $A'+B$ counts heads in $11$ fair flips, which is symmetric about $5.5$, so $P(A'+B\le5)=\frac12$.

**Answer: $\frac12$**

smt-2013-advanced-tiebreaker-02.title: Stars and bars
smt-2013-advanced-tiebreaker-02.body:
Map the letters to $0,\dots,25$. A sequence in alphabetic order is a non-decreasing sequence of $2013$ numbers from $0$ to $25$. It is determined by how many times each letter occurs, i.e. by non-negative integers $n_0,\dots,n_{25}$ with sum $2013$. By stars and bars the number of solutions is $\binom{2013+25}{25}=\binom{2038}{25}$.

**Answer: $\binom{2038}{25}$**

smt-2013-advanced-tiebreaker-03.title: Markov chain on the winning streak
smt-2013-advanced-tiebreaker-03.body:
Let $e_1,e_2$ be the expected number of further games when the current winning streak (by whoever won last) is $1$ or $2$. If the streak holder wins again the streak grows; if she loses the opponent starts a streak of $1$. So

$$e_1=1+\frac12e_2+\frac12e_1,\qquad e_2=1+\frac12\cdot0+\frac12e_1.$$

From the second, $e_2=1+\frac12e_1$; the first gives $\frac12e_1=1+\frac12e_2$, so $e_1=2+e_2=3+\frac12e_1$, hence $e_1=6$ (and $e_2=4$). The first game always creates a streak of $1$, so the expected total is $1+6=7$.

**Answer: 7**
